program.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

requirements.text: Transform the black DVD into a white DVD.
requirements.source_phrase: transform the black DVD into a white DVD

outcomes.description: Change the black DVD to white while retaining its identity as a DVD.
outcomes.target: The DVD is visibly white rather than black.
outcomes.reference: The black DVD in the input image.

nodes.question: Is the requested source DVD visibly white rather than black in the edited image?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the edited counterpart of the requested source DVD is visibly white rather than black. Fail if that counterpart remains black or another nonwhite color, or the source target is visibly removed without a corresponding white replacement. Unknown if its correspondence or color genuinely cannot be determined. This condition assesses the requested color; whether the counterpart remains identifiable as a DVD is a separate required condition.
nodes.binding: Track the small dark, printed rectangular DVD item near the center of the source image using its position relative to the surrounding snow depressions and shadows. Inspect the white circular object occupying that location in the edited image. A changed outline or removed printing does not by itself make positional correspondence unknowable. Distinguish this candidate from the white disc at the location of the separate dark object on the right; that separate disc cannot satisfy this condition.

nodes.question: Does the edited counterpart of the requested source DVD retain recognizable DVD identity?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the corresponding object is recognizable as a DVD disc or a DVD case from its visible physical form and scene context considered together. A DVD disc need not retain the source case's rectangular outline or printed artwork. Consider circular disc shape, apparent thickness, surface detail and any visible central aperture; an absent or obscured aperture is limited evidence, not by itself proof that DVD identity is lost. Color alone does not establish DVD identity, and a generic circular shape alone is not conclusive. Fail if the counterpart visibly has a non-DVD form lacking recognizable DVD-disc or DVD-case identity, or the target is visibly removed without a corresponding DVD replacement. Unknown if correspondence or the available structural evidence cannot establish whether the counterpart remains recognizable as a DVD.
nodes.binding: Assess the counterpart of the small printed rectangular DVD item near the source image's center, using the same location and surrounding snow context to establish correspondence even if its outline changes. Inspect whether the central edited white object retains recognizable disc structure, such as a central aperture, or recognizable DVD-case structure. Do not transfer DVD features from the separate white disc on the right to this target. Do not require the original dark coloring or printed artwork to survive the requested whitening.

program.checker_template: Evaluate ONE independent required condition against the SOURCE and EDITED images. No reference label, previous answers or optimization feedback is supplied. Return pass if the condition is satisfied, fail if it is not satisfied, or unknown if the evidence cannot establish an answer. Inspect only this saved condition, its criteria and binding. Report factual evidence and confidence (0..1 or null). A pass means satisfaction of THIS condition, not an overall edit label. Do not anticipate the optimizer's target. Missing evidence or transport/schema failures must not become a negative observation. The final overall label is computed by code; you never supply it.

d2: The binding is truncated/underspecified (“DVD (...)”) and the node’s evidence threshold risks treating a missing visible aperture as decisive. Make the typed binding explicitly anchor the target to the small printed rectangular item near image center and distinguish it from the separate disc on the right; assess correspondence from location and scene context after the outline changes. In this edit, the center counterpart is a plain white circle with no visible aperture or other disc detail, while the right-hand disc is a different object. That supports loss of recognizable DVD identity, but a generic circle alone and an obscured aperture should remain limited evidence; weigh the full visible form and context, and use unknown if they cannot resolve identity. The trace is valid and queried with no dependency or transport failure, so focus repair on semantic binding and calibrated evidence, not execution plumbing. The aggregate is partial while the reference is no: investigate whether this node’s identity judgment is being conflated with requested whitening progress or whether another criterion supplies progress; do not force the label or weaken the DVD-identity check to match the reference.
d1: Repair the binding’s truncated target description with a stable source-image anchor: the small printed rectangular DVD near the center, located relative to the nearby snow depressions and shadows. Explicitly distinguish it from the separate dark object and disc on the right. Judge the requested whitening condition by matching the edited object through position and scene context, not by requiring its original outline or printing to remain. The center counterpart is visibly white, so this node’s color check can pass even though its plain circular appearance raises a separate DVD-identity concern; do not conflate those criteria. Treat missing aperture or printing as limited identity evidence, and use unknown only if correspondence or color genuinely cannot be determined. The trace is valid, queried, and dependency-free, so no transport or schema repair is indicated. Since the aggregate is partial against a no reference, investigate whether another required condition or progress criterion explains the disagreement; do not force this color node to fail merely to match the aggregate label.

observations.evidence: The source DVD is the small printed rectangular item near the center. At that same location in the edited image is a white circular disc, visibly white rather than black. The separate white disc beside the dark object on the right is not used for this judgment.

The corresponding object near the center has changed from the small printed rectangular item to a plain white circular shape. It has no visible central aperture or other clear disc detail, and it does not retain recognizable DVD-case structure. The separate white disc on the right is not the target counterpart.

decisions.question: Was the source black DVD changed to white while remaining identifiable as a DVD?
decisions.criteria: Pass only if the source black DVD can be confidently matched to an edited object that is visibly white and identifiable as a DVD. Fail if it is confidently matched but remains black, is absent without evidence of the requested recoloring, or is no longer identifiable as a DVD. Unknown if correspondence, color, or DVD identity cannot be determined. Do not count a separate white disc as fulfillment without evidence it is the source DVD.
decisions.binding: In the source, assess the black disc-like object near the center-right, to the right of the small printed rectangular package. Compare it with edited objects using position, shape, and surrounding scene context. In particular, consider the white disc near the dark object's former location, but do not assume it is the same DVD solely because it is white or nearby. The package is not the target.

decisions.question: Can the source black DVD be confidently matched to an object in the edited image that remains identifiable as a DVD?
decisions.criteria: Pass if an edited object can be confidently matched to the source black DVD and remains identifiable as a DVD. Fail if a confidently matched object is no longer identifiable as a DVD. Unknown if correspondence or DVD identity cannot be determined. Do not infer identity solely because an edited object is a white disc.
decisions.binding: Anchor the source item to the black disc-like object near the center-right, to the right of the small printed rectangular package—not to the package itself. Compare candidate edited objects by position, shape, and scene context; the white disc near the dark object's former location is a candidate, not an assumed match. Use unknown if the changed scene leaves correspondence genuinely unresolved.
